proposals: PPAC should publish state-wise monthly volumes of ethanol blended into petrol, so each state’s VAT foregone can be computed from official blending data rather than modelled from petrol consumption at an assumed national E20 level.

The GST Council secretariat should place before the Council an official state-by-state estimate of VAT foregone on ethanol-blended petrol and the SGST returned, so any decision on the ethanol rate is taken against a published figure rather than outside estimates of about ₹17,865 crore.

PPAC should publish annual refinery-wise product slates showing petrol, naphtha and reformate output, so the claim that higher blending frees crude-derived streams for petrochemical feedstock can be quantified rather than argued only directionally.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas should publish the method behind its cumulative figures of 244 lakh tonnes of crude substituted and ₹1.44 lakh crore saved since 2014-15, so the savings can be reproduced and updated each Ethanol Supply Year.
